report.source_text: The patient received 2 g of ceftriaxone and doxycycline 100 mg twice daily. Initial treatment also included an infusion of 0.9% NaCl, 40 mg of esomeprazole once daily, 8 mg of ondansetron twice daily, and 1 g of paracetamol three times daily. Owing to the ECG findings, transcutaneous pacing was initiated at 40 mA with a rhythm maintenance rate of 70 bpm. A dopamine infusion was also administered, starting at 5 mcg/kgBW/minute and later titrated to 10 mcg/kgBW/minute until the systolic blood pressure exceeded 90 mmHg or the mean arterial pressure reached more than 65 mmHg.

report.source_text: Unfortunately, the patient experienced cardiac arrest, and despite ten cycles of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), a return of spontaneous circulation was not achieved. The patient passed away within 48 hours after admission, with cardiogenic shock suspected as the cause of death owing to the deterioration in clinical condition.

clinician.final_diagnosis: The patient was diagnosed with Weil’s disease, complicated by total atrioventricular block (TAVB) and unstable hemodynamics.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old Asian woman presented with worsening chest pain, systemic symptoms (lethargy, anorexia, nausea, fever, headaches), hypotension (81/43 mmHg), and bradycardia (41 bpm). Physical exam revealed anemic conjunctiva, icteric sclera, jaundice, lung crackles, hepatosplenomegaly, and right upper quadrant tenderness. Initial lab tests showed anemia, thrombocytopenia, renal impairment (BUN 92 mg/dL, Creatinine 4.1 mg/dL), liver involvement (AST 102 IU/L, ALT 65 IU/L, Total bilirubin 6.1 mg/dL, Direct bilirubin 5.3 mg/dL), inflammation (CRP 9 mg/dL), and elevated hs-Troponin I (361 ng/dL). Serological tests for leptospirosis (IgM, IgG, MAT) were positive. An ECG revealed total atrioventricular block (TAVB) with a junctional escape rhythm of 45 bpm, with no signs of myocardial infarction. A chest X-ray showed cardiomegaly and increased bronchovascular markings. Initial treatment included ceftriaxone and doxycycline for leptospirosis, transcutaneous pacing for TAVB, and dopamine infusion for hemodynamic support. Despite interventions, the patient experienced cardiac arrest and passed away within 48 hours after admission, with cardiogenic shock suspected as the cause of death.
